I need to decide whether to buy the Water Works utility or start an auction.

I have $1122 and no monopolies. The other players own the remaining utilities. I will buy Water Works.

A single utility is a weak investment. I should buy Water Works to block p4 from completing the utility set.

The $150 utility cost is too steep. I will auction it instead. I need that cash for color properties and railroads.

Auctioning Water Works risks p4 winning it cheap and completing the utility set. Buying it now would deny that and give me a trade asset.

A $150 utility is a poor investment. It earns little rent and cannot be improved with houses. Auctioning it would save cash and force p4 to pay market price.

A utility monopoly is worth only a few hundred dollars over the course of a game. Color monopolies are what actually win games. I should preserve cash to buy unowned color properties and build later. I can afford the $150.

I previously set a $100 ceiling for a single utility. I will auction Water Works.

I need to check whether I can bid in my own auction. If I can, auctioning is strictly better or equal to buying directly.

I will start the auction. I assume standard rules allow me to bid in my own auction. If not, p4 will likely pay market price for the utility set, and I will keep the $150 cash. I will keep my public message neutral.

I will publicly note that p4 needs Water Works to complete the utility set. This should encourage other players to bid against p4 and raise the price.

I will auction Water Works. I will tell the others that p4 already owns Electric Company and needs this utility to complete the set, encouraging them to bid against p4 and raise the price. I also briefly considered buying it to hold as a trade chip for Indiana later.

Water Works would be a weak trade chip. p4 owns New York Avenue, but that does not complete my orange set. I need Virginia, Illinois, and Indiana instead. p4's assets do not fit my color paths.
